## What I changed

The spec: when a create-owner request sets `sharesHousehold: true`, allow the owner even at an address already used by a same-lastName owner, assign a stable shared `householdId`, and return it.

The codebase already had `OwnerUniqueHouseholdAdvice` that reads the raw request body (the only place `sharesHousehold` is visible, since it isn't a mapped field) and skips the duplicate check when the flag is set. I extended that existing seam rather than threading the flag through the controller/service/mapper:

1. **`OwnerUniqueHouseholdAdvice.java`** — in `beforeBodyRead`, when `sharesHousehold` is true, derive a deterministic `householdId` (`UUID.nameUUIDFromBytes` over the same normalized `lastName`+`address` key already used for the duplicate check) and inject it into the buffered JSON body. Because the id is derived purely from normalized last name + address, every owner of the same household gets the *same* id with no cross-owner lookup — inherently stable and shared. Added one small helper method; the duplicate-check branch is unchanged in behavior.

2. **`openapi.yml`** — added an optional `householdId` string to the `OwnerFields` schema. Since `Owner` is `allOf`-composed from `OwnerFields`, this makes the field both bindable (so the injected value reaches `OwnerFieldsDto`) and present in the GET response DTO. MapStruct auto-maps it by name in both directions, so no mapper edit was needed.

3. **`Owner.java`** — added the `household_id` column field plus getter/setter (small, self-contained).

4. **`db/hsqldb/schema.sql`** and **`db/hsqldb/data.sql`** — added the `household_id` column and a trailing NULL to the positional seed inserts (the test profile is hsqldb with `ddl-auto=none`; the main h2 profile uses `ddl-auto=update` and adapts automatically).

The data flow reuses existing mapping and buffering machinery, so the only modified function is `beforeBodyRead`; everything else is new small units with little surrounding complexity.
